name: Markforged Holding Corporation (MarkForged, Inc.)
subcategory: composite (continuous carbon fibre) FFF and bound-metal 3D printers, 'Digital Forge' platform
origin_detail: Founded 2013 by Gregory Mark and CTO David Benhaim; launched the Mark One continuous-carbon-fibre printer at SolidWorks World 2014. Seed from North Bridge and Matrix (2013); later Microsoft Ventures (M12), Porsche SE, Trinity, Next47 and Summit Partners. Based in the Boston area (Watertown, later Waltham, MA).
flagship_projects: Mark One / Mark Two (continuous carbon fibre FFF, 2014/2016)
PX100 metal binder jetting (from Digital Metal)
Eiger cloud software / The Digital Forge (2020)
openness_notes: Closed from launch: proprietary printers and materials, cloud-connected 'proprietary software' (FY2024 10-K: 'Our proprietary software provides a single platform to interact with many of our hardware devices', covering Simulation, Inspection, Performance Advisor and Digital Source), and a patent portfolio of 71 US and 94 foreign issued patents (2024). The Wikipedia article and the fetched filings mention no open-source origin (e.g. no RepRap lineage). Scored 0 at both dates.

license_history.note: Closed from the Mark One onward
71 US + 94 foreign issued patents, 61 pending or allowed

exit_events.counterparty: one (SPAC sponsored by A-star, led by Kevin Hartz; NYSE: AONE)
exit_events.note: Announced 2021-02-24 at an implied pro forma equity value of ~$2.1B, with a ~$210M PIPE (Baron, BlackRock, Miller Value, Wasatch, Wellington, M12, Porsche) and up to $425M gross proceeds, on ~$70M 2020 revenue; closed 2021-07-14, NYSE: MKFG.

Agreement 2024-09-25 at $5.00 cash per share (after a 1-for-10 reverse split in Sept 2024); CFIUS investigation; closed 2025-04-25, NYSE delisting and Form 15-12G (2025-05-09). Wikipedia values the transaction at $116M.

Announced 2026-05-27: Nano Dimension to sell MarkForged, Inc. (FFF/composites business, ~$70M 2025 revenue including the metal binder jetting line that Nano keeps) to Stratasys for $42.5M cash; closing expected 2H 2026 (not confirmed as closed).

risk_events: 2018: sued by Desktop Metal over metal-printing patents and alleged IP theft; a July 2018 ruling favoured Markforged
Jul 2021: listed via the 'one' SPAC at ~$2.1B implied equity value on ~$70M revenue
Apr 2024: jury verdict of $17.3M for Continuous Composites (patent case); Sept 2024 settlement with $18M paid 2024-10-10 plus $1M/$2M/$4M due in Q4 2025-2027, secured on patent rights
2023-2024: revenue fell from $93.8M to $85.1M with net losses of $103.6M and $85.6M; 1-for-10 reverse split effective 2024-09-19
Apr 2025: taken private by Nano Dimension at $5.00/share (~$116M); CEO Shai Terem and CFO resigned
May 2026: resold to Stratasys for $42.5M, about 2% of the 2021 SPAC equity value (my arithmetic)
robustness: Low as an independent entity: two changes of owner in about a year, with the composites business heading into Stratasys and the binder-jetting line staying with Nano Dimension. Customers rely on closed, cloud-connected software and proprietary consumables, so continuity depends on the new owner's support decisions. An installed base in '10,000 facilities across 70 countries' (2021) gives the acquirer a reason to keep supporting it.
physical_science_relevance: Not a laser powder-bed fusion vendor. Its metal line (Metal X: 17-4 PH, copper, H13, Inconel 625, D2; FX10 Metal Kit; PX100 binder jetting) is extrusion- or binder-based plus sintering, and it offers no aluminium alloy; its continuous-carbon-fibre parts are marketed to 'replace machined aluminum parts'. Relevant to a lab mainly for strong fixtures, grippers and enclosures for automated rigs, not for alloy development. Closed cloud software limits scripted, self-driving-lab use.
openness_effect_assessment: Markforged was closed by design and relied on patents both offensively and defensively; the patent strategy cost it a $17.3M verdict and an ~$25M settlement in 2024. Openness had no visible role in its rise (SPAC at ~$2.1B) or fall (resold for $42.5M in 2026); the decline tracked weak revenue growth, losses and post-SPAC re-pricing rather than licensing choices.
key_takeaway: Markforged is a SPAC-era closed-hardware story: about $137M of venture money and a ~$2.1B SPAC valuation in 2021, then a 1-for-10 reverse split, a patent loss, a $116M take-private by Nano Dimension in 2025 and a $42.5M resale to Stratasys in 2026. Its proprietary, cloud-tied printers changed hands twice in thirteen months, which is the vendor-continuity risk a lab takes on when it buys closed AM hardware.

firmware_software_licenses: Proprietary (Eiger / Digital Forge cloud software, firmware)
hardware_extras.patents: 71 US and 94 foreign issued patents, 61 pending or allowed (FY2024 10-K); >170 issued and pending (Feb 2021). Lost a 2024 jury verdict ($17.3M) to Continuous Composites and settled; won a 2018 ruling against Desktop Metal.
